subject: digital-logic
subtopics: Boolean algebra postulates (closure, identity elements, commutativity, the two distributive laws, complement) and the count of Boolean functions 2^(2^n)
duality: the dual of an expression, self-dual functions and the count 2^(2^(n-1))
the working theorems: idempotent, involution, domination, absorption, De Morgan and consensus
XOR and XNOR algebra: the identities, associativity, and where XOR differs from OR
canonical forms: minterms, maxterms, Sigma m and Pi M, and conversion between canonical SOP and POS
the algebraic minimisation technique: combine, absorb, eliminate, factor and multiply out
Karnaugh map layout: Gray-code ordering, cell numbering, adjacency and wrap-around
grouping rules and reading a product term off a group (pair, quad, octet; prime implicants)
essential prime implicants and the minimal cover, including functions with several minimal SOPs
don't-care conditions: X as 0 or 1, in SOP and in POS, and the rule that X never makes a prime implicant essential
POS minimisation: grouping the zeros and reading sum terms with inverted polarity
the five-variable map: two four-variable maps, the reflection axis and the overlay view
the tabular (Quine-McCluskey) method: grouping by number of 1s, dash combination, the prime implicant chart, essential rows, dominance and cyclic charts
cost: literals, terms, gate counts and the n - k literal rule

chosen.title: Lecture 07 - Fundamentals of Boolean Algebra
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits (Prof. Goutam Saha, IIT Kharagpur)
covers: the 16 functions of two variables and the 2^(2^n) count
the six Huntington postulates, including the second distributive law
the duality rule, with the 0/1 and OR/AND swap
the closing warning that AND and OR are associative and distributive over each other while NAND and NOR are not
chosen.why: The only readable lecture this run that derives the postulates one by one in the lecturer's own order and then states the duality rule as a working tool rather than a slogan. It is also the source of the function-count argument (2^n rows, each output free), which is the one counting result GATE keeps asking. Its closing summary supplies the NAND/NOR associativity contrast that GATE CSE 2019 Q.6 turns on. The served transcript stops before the worked theorem derivations, so those are recomputed here instead of quoted.

chosen.title: Lecture 10 - Karnaugh Map and Digital Circuit Realization
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits (Prof. Goutam Saha, IIT Kharagpur)
covers: truth table to grid, with the axis labels read as variables
minterm numbering m0..m3 in the two-variable map
the first grouping, AB' + AB = A

the closing summary: adjacency is the method; SOP covers every 1 with the fewest and largest power-of-two groups; POS covers the 0s; a don't care is taken as 0 or 1 according to which enlarges the group
the introduction of the dual circuit and the self-dual function
chosen.why: The closest readable match to the syllabus words 'Karnaugh map': it builds the map from the truth table and then states the four grouping rules in a closing summary that is exactly the checklist the cards use. No other readable source states the SOP-cover and POS-cover rules in one place, and its don't-care rule is the one both don't-care cards rest on.

chosen.title: Lecture 11 - Karnaugh Map to Entered Variable Map
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits (Prof. Goutam Saha, IIT Kharagpur)
covers: 32 cells for five variables
two four-variable maps with the fifth variable fixed at 0 and at 1
the reflection axis, with cells 3 and 7 and cells 1 and 5 as the lecturer's adjacency examples
the overlay alternative and the closing statement that five-variable adjacency needs three-dimensional visualisation
chosen.why: The only readable source that constructs the five-variable map rather than asserting its layout. The reflection argument - a cell is adjacent to the cell 16 places away because only the fifth variable changes - is what the five-variable card teaches, and it is the lecturer's own worked adjacency pair rather than a reconstruction.

chosen.title: Lecture 12 - Quine-McCluskey (QM) Algorithm
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits (Prof. Goutam Saha, IIT Kharagpur)
covers: the three steps: prime implicants, essential prime implicants, minimal set
implicant and prime implicant defined
grouping minterms by the number of 1s, and the iterative combination
the closing rule that don't cares are included when finding prime implicants and excluded when finding essential prime implicants
chosen.why: The syllabus names the 'tabular method' explicitly and this is the readable lecture on it. Its closing rule about don't cares is the exact distinction GATE CSE 2018 Q.49 is built on, and no other source read this run states it in that form. The stage-1 table of its four-variable example is quoted; the chart stage is taken from the written reference instead.

chosen.title: Karnaugh map
covers: Gray-code ordering so that adjacent cells differ in one variable
power-of-two rectangles that may overlap
toroidal connectivity and the wrap-around groups
the reading rule: keep the variables constant across the box and drop the rest
don't cares that may be included or excluded from a group
the POS obtained by minimising the complement and applying De Morgan
chosen.why: Used as the standard reference for the two facts the cards state most often and that no lecture read this run states cleanly: the toroidal (wrap-around) adjacency, and the reading rule for a group. It is also the second voice on the POS-by-complement route, so that no card's POS claim rests on one page.

chosen.title: Quine-McCluskey algorithm
covers: the algorithm's two phases and its equivalence to the map
a four-variable worked example with two don't cares, showing the grouping by number of 1s and the dash notation
the prime implicant chart, and the essential prime implicants read off as columns with a single tick
the complexity note: the chart stage is a set-cover problem
chosen.why: The lecture gives the grouping stage but its chart stage was not served, and the chart is the half of the method that GATE's counting questions need. This reference supplies the chart and the single-tick rule, and its worked example is the only place read this run where a don't care is carried through the table explicitly.

chosen.title: Minimization of Switching Functions (Unit II instructional material)
chosen.channel: Aditya Engineering College, digital logic course notes
covers: logical adjacency defined as differing in one literal
the six grouping rules and the 'loneliest square first' advice
implicant, prime implicant, essential prime implicant and cover defined
the three-step minimal-SOP algorithm
the five-variable map layout and a five-variable worked function
the tabular method's two phases, the cover table, distinguished columns, row and column dominance and the cyclic cover table
the cost criteria: fewest literals, fewest terms
chosen.why: The only readable source that covers the tabular method's chart stage with dominance and the cyclic case, which the lecture did not reach and Wikipedia mentions only in passing. It also supplies the cost vocabulary (fewest literals, fewest terms) that the literal-count card needs, and it states the essential-prime-implicant definition in the form the 2018 question tests.

chosen.title: K-Map in Hindi - what a K-map is, with examples
covers: cells number 2^n and are numbered in Gray code
minterms for SOP and maxterms for POS
1s grouped for SOP and 0s grouped for POS
pairs, quads and octets, with one variable removed per doubling
overlapping groups, and edge cells joined by rolling the map
chosen.why: Chosen deliberately so the topic is not built from English alone, and the only readable non-English source found this run. It is a Hindi-medium treatment of the same grouping rules, and it names the pair/quad/octet ladder and the rolling of the map in Hindi, which is how a large part of the GATE audience first meets the method. Every sentence taken from it is translated here and marked as translated on the cards that use it; it contributes terminology and the grouping ladder, not any number.

chosen.title: Digital Logic subject notes: K Map, MSOP and MPOS
chosen.channel: GATE Overflow, subject page for Digital Logic
covers: the grouping rules in GATE's own phrasing
prime implicant and essential prime implicant defined
the don't-care rule
the three-step minimal-SOP algorithm and the MPOS derivation from the zeros
the paper-by-paper mark distribution for Digital Logic, used to check which years asked this topic
chosen.why: The GATE-oriented statement of the rules, used to phrase the cards the way the exam phrases the question and to check the subtopic enumeration against the questions actually asked. It is a revision text, not a lecture, so nothing is attributed to it that is not a definition or a rule.

standard_refs: M. Morris Mano and Michael D. Ciletti, Digital Design, chapter 2 (Boolean algebra and logic gates) and chapter 3 (gate-level minimisation: the map method, four- and five-variable maps, don't-care conditions, NAND and NOR implementation, the tabulation method) - the reference the NPTEL Digital Electronic Circuits course itself lists
Donald P. Leach, Albert P. Malvino and Goutam Saha, Digital Principles and Applications, the Boolean algebra and minimisation chapters
Thomas L. Floyd, Digital Fundamentals, the Boolean analysis and combinational logic chapters
GATE 2027 CS syllabus, Digital Logic line 'Boolean algebra and minimization - algebraic technique, Karnaugh map, tabular method'
notes: The syllabus names this topic in one line of eight words, so the fourteen subtopics above are this run's enumeration from the standard treatment (Mano chapters 2-3, the NPTEL lecture order, the GATE question record) and not a quotation from the syllabus. The three techniques the line names - algebraic, map, tabular - are the spine; the rest are the sub-skills each one needs.

Twelve GATE CSE previous-year questions were verified, from 1998 to 2026, and every one is SOURCED against an accepted answer rather than key-verified against an official paper, so no marks field is recorded. One secondary page attributes the answer 3 of GATE CSE 2018 Q.49 to the official key, which is noted in that record and not relied on.

Functional completeness (NAND and NOR as universal gates, and the completeness tests) is not carded here: the repository already carries it as content/subjects/discrete-mathematics/propositional-logic/functional-completeness.json, and one concept gets one card at one path. That card, not this topic, is where the completeness tests live.
Gray code is carded here, as the number-systems source ledger promised it would be: it is the ordering rule of the map and the reason adjacency works.

The entered-variable map (EVM), multiple-output minimisation, static and dynamic hazards, and the cost criteria beyond literal counting are taught by the chosen NPTEL lectures (11 and 13) but are outside the eight words of the syllabus line and are not carded. They are named here so a later run does not think they were missed.

The one non-English source is a Hindi K-map chapter (ehindistudy). Its contribution is the grouping ladder, the rolling of the map and the pair/quad/octet naming, all translated into English and marked as translated on the cards that use them. No Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali lecture transcript was readable this run.

No video transcript was readable: the Gate Smashers playlist that matches this topic lecture for lecture is recorded as structure only, and videoRefs is empty on every card. That is a gap, not a claim.

The visual lesson animates one map end to end - GATE CSE 2014 Set 3 Q.7's function - because the order of the steps is the difficulty: place the 1s, place the don't cares, let a don't care join a group, read the constant variables, then check that leaving the don't cares out would have cost four 4-literal terms. Its cells and terms are recomputed in scripts/validate.py.
